answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks using hardware-anchored remote attestation. Each agent must present a cryptographic proof signed by a secure enclave, creating a basalt root of physical provenance to withstand any gale of automated registrations. An adversary incurs the verifiable capital cost of provisioning discrete, vendor-certified silicon per identity. However, side-channel attacks can extract signing keys, degrading verification into a porous karst of undetected counterfeits.
